{{nihongo|'''Sanuki Shrine'''|讃岐神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

'''Sanuki Shrine''' (さぬきじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Miyoshi, {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|Q1346830|qid=Q1346830}}, {{ill|Kitakatsuragi District, Nara|Q1131013|qid=Q1131013}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Nara|af|Nara-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Nara|ar|نارا (محافظة)|az|Nara prefekturası|azb|نارا اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Nara|bat_smg|Naras prefektūra|be|Нара (прэфектура)|bg|Нара (префектура)|bn|নারা প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Nara|cdo|Nara-gâing|ce|Нара (префектура)|ceb|Nara-ken|ckb|پارێزگای نارا|cs|Prefektura Nara|cy|Nara (talaith)|da|Nara-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Nara|eo|Gubernio Nara|es|Prefectura de Nara|et|Nara prefektuur|eu|Nara (prefektura)|fa|استان نارا|fi|Naran prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Nara|frr|Nara (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Nara|gl|Prefectura de Nara|gor|Prefektur Nara|hak|Nara-yen|he|נארה (מחוז)|hr|Nara (prefektura)|hu|Nara prefektúra|hy|Նարա (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Nara|ilo|Prepektura ti Nara|it|Prefettura di Nara|ja|奈良県|jv|Préfèktur Nara|ka|ნარის პრეფექტურა|kk|Нара (префектура)|km|ណារ៉ា(ខេត្ត)|ko|나라현|la|Naraënsis|lt|Naros prefektūra|lv|Naras prefektūra|mk|Нара (префектура)|mni|ꯅꯥꯔꯥ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|नारा प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Nara|my|နာရခရိုင်|nl|Nara (prefectuur)|no|Nara (prefektur)|os|Нарæ (префектурæ)|pam|Prepektura ning Nara|pl|Prefektura Nara|pnb|ضلع نارا|pt|Nara (prefeitura)|ro|Prefectura Nara|ru|Нара (префектура)|sco|Nara Prefectur|sd|نارا پريفيڪچر|se|Nara prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Nara|si|නාරා ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Nara Prefecture|sk|Nara (prefektúra)|sl|Prefektura Nara|sr|Префектура Нара|su|Nara Prefecture|sv|Nara prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Nara|ta|நாரா மாநிலம்|tg|Префектураи Нара|th|จังหวัดนาระ|tl|Prepektura ng Nara|tok|ma Nala|tr|Nara (prefektörlük)|tt|Нара (префектура)|uk|Префектура Нара|ur|نارا پریفیکچر|vi|Nara (tỉnh)|war|Nara (prefektura)|wuu|奈良县|zh|奈良县|zh_classical|奈良縣|zh_min_nan|Nara-koān|zh_yue|奈良縣|qid=Q131287}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=old shrine ranking}} it was a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

Because the "old bamboo cutter" in '{{ill|The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter|Q923593|qid=Q923593}}' is named "Sanuki no Miyatsuko," the shrine presents itself as one related to the tale, identifying this with Sanuki in Hirose District of Yamato<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|和書 |title=History of Kōryō Town (main volume) |date=2001-5-31 |publisher=Kōryō Town |pages=1125-1139 |author=Kōryō Town}}</ref>.

=== Enshrined deities ===
Currently it enshrines {{ill|Kunitama|Q9692242|qid=Q9692242|lt=Ōkunitama-no-Mikoto}}, Waka-uka-no-me-no-Mikoto, and {{ill|Ōmononushi|lt=Ōmononushi|Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi-no-Mikoto}}.
In '{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}},' entry for {{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}} 7 ({{ill|883|Q30355|qid=Q30355}}), 12th month, 2nd day, it says "bestow Junior Fifth Lower rank on Sankichi Ōtate-no-Mikoto and Sankichi Inoki deity," thought to refer to this shrine's deities.

=== History ===
The place name "Miyoshi" is read "Mitsuyoshi" now, but it was formerly written "Sankichi" and read "Sanuki." This area is thought to have been settled by the {{ill|Inbe clan|fa|خاندان اینبه|ja|忌部氏|pl|Inbe (ród)|simple|Inbe clan|th|ตระกูลอิมเบะ|zh|忌部氏|qid=Q8189229|lt=Imibe clan}} of {{ill|Sanuki Province|Q929682|qid=Q929682}}, who invited the deity of their homeland and founded the shrine. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as "Sanuki Shrine, Hirose District, {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}," ranked as a small shrine.

Because Waka-uka-no-me-no-Mikoto of Hirose Kawai (present {{ill|Hirose Taisha|Q705281|qid=Q705281}}) was invited, until the Edo period it was called "Hirose Daimyōjin" and "Minami Kawai Myōjin." A fire occurred in {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 19 ({{ill|1611|Q6768|qid=Q6768}}), first month; the current honden was rebuilt at that time.

=== Sanuki Shrine and The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter ===
There are multiple theories about the setting of '{{ill|The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter|Q923593|qid=Q923593}}' (the Kaguya-hime legend), often called Japan's oldest narrative, and Kōryō in Kitakatsuragi District, Nara Prefecture, is said to be a strong candidate.

'''Reasons Kōryō is said to be the setting'''<ref name=":0" />
* The old bamboo cutter's name is '''Sanuki no Miyatsuko''' - opening of the tale: "Long ago there was an old bamboo cutter ... his name was called Sanuki no Miyatsuko."
* The old man's name indicates he was the head of the Sanuki lineage living in the Yamato locality called '''Sankichi (Sanuki)'''.
* In the Heian-period "Engishiki," the location of the Shikinaisha Sanuki Shrine is written as '''Sankichi-gō, Hirose District, Yamato Province''', corresponding to '''Miyoshi, Kōryō, Kitakatsuragi District, Nara'''.

=== Film location ===
[[ファイル:奈良県_広陵町_讃岐神社_ロケ地表示.jpg|サムネイル|Sanuki Shrine filming-location sign]]
It was selected as one filming location for the movie '{{ill|Library with Angels|Q28943614|qid=Q28943614}},' set in Nara's Katsuragi area ({{ill|Yamatotakada, Nara|Q838669|qid=Q838669}}, {{ill|Gose, Nara|Q847334|qid=Q847334}}, {{ill|Kashiba, Nara|Q696643|qid=Q696643}}, {{ill|Katsuragi, Nara|Q659672|qid=Q659672}}, {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|Q1346830|qid=Q1346830}})<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.toshokan-movie.com/|title=Japanese film "Tenshi no Iru Toshokan"|access-date=2017-2-11}}</ref>. Starring: {{ill|Fuka Koshiba|Q11463509|qid=Q11463509}}; co-starring: {{ill|Ryusei Yokohama|Q15876471|qid=Q15876471}}.
